messages.subject: Re: Problems computing posterior predictives
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

Is there a way around setting test = "none"? This is because fitMeasures do not work when this done and I can't get PPP values for my model.

I'm using a Windows 10 Desktop, R version 3.5.0, blavaan 0.3-4, and rstan  version 2.18.2. Even with no parallel computing and R version 3.6.0, "Computing posterior predictives" looks like it's running forever.

Thanks,
John

messages.subject: Re: Problems computing posterior predictives
messages.body_plain:
John

If you set test="none", you will not get any value that comes from the log-likelohoods (or marginal LL). This is because you are asking to skip that step

Factors that affect the time of calculation: complexity of your model, sample size, number of saved samples, missing data. You cannot change the model or sample size, you can control the number of saved samples, if you are now saving 10000 samples per chain, I would recommend to change it to 2000 for example, this was the posterior predictive calculation time will be shorter

messages.subject: error received from blavFitIndices function
messages.body_plain:
I would like to examine model fit indices for a parallel growth curve model I have run but when I use the blavFitIndices function on my model object, I receive the following error (thousands of times, it seems):

Error in pd.solve(varcov, log.det = TRUE) : NA's in x

Additional information: the model had a difficult time converging. I estimated the model using 50,000 iterations of HMC with a burn-in period of 25,000 before trace and autocorrelation plots looked okay. PPP = 000, which is why I would like to examine other fit indices (BRMSEA, BCFI) for comparison.

Any recommendations?

Thanks,

Matt

messages.subject: Re: error received from blavFitIndices function
messages.body_plain:
> I receive the following error (thousands of times, it seems):
>
> Error in pd.solve(varcov, log.det = TRUE) : NA's in x

Mauricio and I don't use solve() for anything in our implementation, so I'm guessing you changed the defaults to use rescale = "ppmc".  That is the only situation where I can imagine inversion happening, probably during data generation from model parameters for posterior predictive modeling checking.  Do you have a NPD theta or psi matrix?

> Additional information: the model had a difficult time converging. I estimated the model using 50,000 iterations of HMC with a burn-in period of 25,000 before trace and autocorrelation plots looked okay. PPP = 000, which is why I would like to examine other fit indices (BRMSEA, BCFI) for comparison.

Wow, NUTS in Stan shouldn't take so long to converge, but that's why you get the message thousands of times.  In my fork of the development version, I just added a "thin" argument you could set to 500 to speed up the process considerably and still base the results on 500 samples, but that would only be useful if PPMC didn't run into this error.

I would try running it with the default rescale="DevM", which does not require any PPMC information.

https://doi.org/10.1037/met0000224

https://osf.io/afkcw/

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.subject: Re: error received from blavFitIndices function
messages.body_plain:
You could easily fit your model with ML in lavaan, at least to get an idea about fit.  I think you would get 5 df from covariance structure and 2 df from mean structure restrictions, so you could also use the lavResiduals() function (also works with blavaan models, but treats posterior SDs as SEs and calculates z statistics, which you can ignore in the Bayes context) to see what the standardized residuals are.  You would also get a z test for the SRMR for mean and covariance structure, separately and combined in the $summary table, but again those are frequentist statistics calculated using Bayesian quantities.  Again, this would just give you an idea what the problems might be with your model.

I notice your intercepts and slopes are basically zero, so the mean begins at zero, and then doesn't change of the (merely 3) occasions.  Did you mean center your 6 indicators?  If so, that doesn't leave anything for your model to explain, except some interindividual variability in intraindividual change (i.e., covariance structure parameters).  An overparameterized model might be the problem...

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
